transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. Patel. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, Dr. Patel. Well, I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble with my eating. 

What really scares me is that once I start eating—especially when I’m alone in the kitchen—it feels like I’ve just stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop. Even though I'm telling myself the whole time, ‘Janet, put it away,’ I just can't seem to do it. It's like I have no control over it at all.
After these episodes of eating where you feel like you can't stop, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, exercising a lot, or using laxatives?
No, I don't do anything like that. I've never tried to make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or... or exercise a bunch afterwards. I just don't do anything to try and undo it.
How often do these episodes happen where you feel like you can't stop eating, and do they happen even when you're not alone?

Well, looking back at my kitchen calendar and my food bank weeks, I'd say they've been happening most weeks. Usually it's once or twice a week, and it's been going on like that for many months now. 

As for when other people are around... no, not really. It's pretty much always when I'm by myself. I don't think I could do it in front of anyone else.
When you’re eating during these episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control, like you can’t stop eating even if you want to?
Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it feels like I have absolutely no control. Even when I'm telling myself to stop, I just... I can't. I just keep going.
Do you feel a lot of distress or upset about these episodes of eating where you can’t stop, even though you don’t try to compensate for them afterwards?

Yes, I really do. Afterward, I just feel awful about myself. I sit there and realize I've wasted food that I actually meant to share or save. And... well, I'm 48, so I feel like I'm way too old to be acting this way. I usually just sit there feeling completely ashamed, and I always promise myself that it won't happen again.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?

Yes, I definitely do. I catch myself eating so fast that I barely even taste the food. Like if I made a casserole or baked some muffins, I'll just stand right there at the kitchen counter taking bite after bite. It's like I'm in a huge hurry to get it all down, even when there's absolutely nowhere I need to be.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Well, like I said a little bit ago... yes. That's actually what scares me the most about it. Once I start eating, especially if I'm just standing there alone in the kitchen, it's like I've stepped aside or something. I can't make myself stop. The whole time, in my head, I'm telling myself, "Janet, put it away, just stop," but I just can't do it.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely eat a lot during those times, but I wouldn't say I get to the point where my stomach hurts or I feel sick from being too full. It's more about the feeling of losing control than the physical feeling of being stuffed, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food even when you’re not physically hungry during these episodes?

Yes, definitely. A lot of times this happens after I've already had supper. My stomach isn't asking for anything, I'm not actually hungry at all, but I still go back to the pantry or the fridge. I'll just start picking at things, and before I know it, it turns into a lot of food.
Do you ever find yourself starting to eat even when you know you’re not physically hungry at all?

Yeah, like I was just saying, yes. I'll start eating even when I know I'm not physically hungry at all. It's just like I mentioned about going back to the kitchen after supper. My body isn't asking for food, but I start eating anyway.
Do these episodes of feeling like you can’t stop eating usually happen when you’re feeling stressed, anxious, sad, or upset about something?

I don't really think so. I haven't noticed a connection, anyway. I mean, I don't feel particularly stressed or sad when it happens. It just sort of... happens, even on a completely normal, quiet evening. I wouldn't say being upset is what sets it off.
Can you recall if you start eating during these episodes even when you know you’re not physically hungry at all?
Well, like I said before, yes. I do start eating even when I'm not hungry. It's just like I was explaining about eating after supper when I'm already full.
Do you eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much food you're consuming?

No, I don't think so. I mean, sometimes I happen to be by myself when I eat like that, but I'm not... I'm not doing it on purpose to hide from anyone. I wouldn't say I'm eating alone just because I'm embarrassed about the amount of food. It's just not really a factor for me.

This supports Binge Eating Disorder (F50.2) and rules out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.0) due to absence of compensatory behaviors.

These details continue to support both Binge Eating Disorder (F50.2) and Eating Disorder Not Otherwise Specified (F50.0). No additional features were identified to distinguish between the two more clearly.
